newsitem.title: TURKEY: Hoechst's Turkish JV aims $120-mln exports.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst's Turkish JV aims $120-mln exports.

text.p: A 50-50 joint venture between German chemical group Hoechst and Turkey's industrial conglomerate Sabanci Holding is aiming exports worth $120 million annually, senior officials said.

"The company will be the biggest in its field in Europe," said Sakip Sabanci, president of Sabanci Holding, at the ground-breaking ceremony for the HoecSa, to be built in the industrial city of Izmit, to the east of Istanbul
"Its sales revenue from June 1999, when it will become operational, will be $150 million, of which $120 million is exports," he told the ceremony.
The plant, which will have an investment cost of 166 million German marks, will annually produce 14,000 tonnes of polyester yarn and 12,000 tonnes of cord fabric and will employ 250 people, he said.
He said exports would go to Europe, Africa, Middle East and India.
Justus Mische, a member of executive committee of Hoechst, told the ceremony that the joint venture would use the state-or-the-art technology for production.
"Hoechst and Sabanci will also cooperate in other areas," he said.
